newsitem.title: USA: Cigarette fire kills four children, two adults.
newsitem.headline: Cigarette fire kills four children, two adults.

text.p: Four children and two adults died in a house fire early Sunday that officials said was caused by a carelessly discarded cigarette.

A third adult who survived by leaping from the top floor of the three-story row house in southwest Philadelphia was recovering in a local hospital. Another man, Ronald Davenport, 37, died trying to escape the same way. The injured man was named as Mark Bonner, 26.
Police said four children aged between 11 months and six years, and a 23-year-old woman were found dead in their beds by firefighters who were called out about 5:30 a.m. EDT.

The woman was named as Fatima Bonner and the children as Sherrell Bonner, 6, Kareem Fittimon, 4, Kiara Fittimon, 2, and Devon Letherburry, 11 months. Their relationship was not established, the fire official said, but the rowhouse was a single-family dwelling.
Fire marshal Lt. Tom Lawson said the fire started when a discarded cigarette ignited a sofa on the first floor.
Fire Commissioner Harold Hairston said the family might have been saved by smoke detectors. "We were told the house was equipped, but we could not find them," he said.
